title: How Forward Deployed Engineering is done at Factory — Eno Reyes
talk_summary: Eno Reyes describes Factory's forward-deployed engineering model, where deployed engineers feed customer signal back into the product and help customers build 'software factories' — signal-to-deploy pipelines with no human interruption. The core technical claim is that agent autonomy scales with 'agent readiness': the density of deterministic validation loops (linters, type checkers, tests, security scans) in a codebase, since these provide the dense reward signals long-running agents need.

takeaways.technique: Agent readiness = density of deterministic validators
takeaways.what_they_do: They measure how many deterministic validation loops (linters, type checkers, security scans, tests) exist in a codebase and treat that count as the predictor of how long agents can run autonomously without human intervention.
takeaways.evidence_quote: what agent readiness really is is it's a measure of how many of these deterministic validation loops are present inside of your code base

takeaways.what_they_do: Before running a long autonomous task, they define what 'complete' means as a set of verification systems; the harness then 'pushes a lever of inference' until those validators pass, with humans only at the planning stage.
They track the ratio of actions done by humans to AI actions before a human interruption, and separately what fraction of work is autonomous, to know where the harness is actually closing loops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: our autonomy ratio is like in the upper 80%, which means the ratio of actions done by humans to AI systems before interruption
takeaways.numbers: ~15-20% of their own work autonomous; autonomy ratio in upper 80%

takeaways.technique: Bounded long-running 'missions' with planning-only human gate
takeaways.what_they_do: Long-running harnesses where a human scopes a bounded, verifiable task once, then inference runs to completion with almost no further intervention.
takeaways.evidence_quote: it's simply a long running harness that has almost no human intervention except for the planning stage

takeaways.what_they_do: They deliberately keep the agent harness model-agnostic and retain all traces/data flowing through it, arguing vendor lock-in to one model is both expensive and constrains what you can build.

takeaways.technique: Make the codebase 'agent ready' beyond 30-40% auto-fixable
takeaways.what_they_do: They note only 30-40% of readiness gaps are one-click fixable by the agent; the rest need workflow changes and human buy-in, so they treat readiness as an org change, not a tool run.
takeaways.evidence_quote: for I'd say maybe 30 to 40% of the low-hanging fruit, you click droid, please fix all of this
takeaways.numbers: 30-40% of readiness fixes are one-click automatable
